text: The cold-chain controller shall keep stored vaccine within 2 to 8 degrees C and say, with a stated error, how long it will stay there.
The plant model shall be checked against independent references before any controller result is trusted.
rationale: A controller verified against a wrong plant is verified against nothing.

text: With the compressor off and no door openings, the stepped plant temperature shall match the closed-form first-order solution to within 1e-9 degrees C over 10000 minutes.
acceptance: C-PLANT-EXACT: max absolute difference over 10000 one-minute steps is at most 1e-9 C, for 100 random (T0, Ta, tau) triples.

text: The plant parameters shall be fitted from a recorded step test, and the fitted model shall predict a held-out section of the same recording.
acceptance: C-PLANT-FIT: on a recording split 70/30 by time, RMS prediction error on the held-out 30 percent is at most 0.3 C.
rationale: Offline this runs on synthetic recordings with known parameters; beyond the lab it runs on a real fridge. The 0.3 C bound is a placeholder until a reference thermometer's own error is known.

text: The controller shall hold the band under door openings and protect the compressor.
Over 1000 simulated 30-day runs with powered compressor and seeded door openings, the simulated product temperature shall stay within 2 to 8 degrees C.
acceptance: C-CTL-BAND: zero runs with any minute outside [2, 8] C; the worst-case maximum and minimum are recorded as TPMs.
rationale: Spike: 24 h gave max 7.04 C with hysteresis 3 to 6 C, so the margin is under 1 C and must be watched, not assumed.

text: The controller shall never restart the compressor less than 3 minutes after stopping it.
acceptance: C-CTL-SHORTCYCLE: across all C-CTL-BAND runs, the minimum off-interval before any restart is at least 3 minutes.
rationale: Short-cycling damages compressors. The 3-minute figure is a common default, to be replaced by the compressor maker's number.

text: The controller shall process every sensor reading it is sent, in order, with none dropped.
acceptance: C-CTL-NOLOSS: 10000 readings injected, including bursts of 50 at one instant, give 10000 processed readings in injection order and putsWaiting returns to 0.
rationale: des README decision 11: a signal() loop drops simultaneous injections. The controller uses subscribe().

text: With two probes, the controller shall raise a sensor-fault alarm when they disagree by more than 1 degree C for 10 consecutive minutes, or when one reports an unchanged value for 60 minutes.
acceptance: C-CTL-SENSOR: each of 4 injected faults (stuck, offset +2 C, drift 0.05 C per min, dropout) is alarmed within 70 minutes, and 1000 fault-free 30-day runs raise zero sensor alarms.
rationale: The instrument is the commonest liar. A controller that trusts one probe controls the probe, not the vaccine.

text: The controller shall raise an excursion alarm within 5 minutes of the simulated product temperature leaving 2 to 8 degrees C.
acceptance: C-CTL-ALARM: in 500 seeded runs with forced excursions (door left open, power cut, compressor failure), every alarm is raised at most 5 minutes after the excursion starts, and no run has an excursion without an alarm.
rationale: An excursion nobody hears about is the expensive kind.

text: During a power cut, the controller shall forecast time until the 8 degrees C limit by simulating ahead from the current state.
rationale: The decision a clinic actually faces: move the stock now, or wait for power.

text: With no door openings, the holdover forecast shall agree with the closed-form time to 8 degrees C to within one time step.
acceptance: C-FC-EXACT: for 100 random starting temperatures in [2, 7.9] C, the absolute difference from tau times ln((Ta - T0) / (Ta - 8)) is at most dt.
rationale: Spike: 71 min simulated against 70.67 min closed form with dt = 1 min.

text: The holdover forecast's low quantile shall be calibrated: its stated p10 shall be exceeded by the true holdover in 90 percent of cases, give or take sampling error.
acceptance: C-FC-CAL: over 2000 held-out simulated outages from a hidden truth model, the fraction with true holdover at least the forecast p10 lies in [0.87, 0.93].
rationale: For a move-or-wait decision the useful number is a low quantile; p80 of time-to-breach is the optimistic one. At n = 2000 one binomial standard error is 0.0067, so this interval is about ±4.5 SE, not ±3. It is wide on purpose: the truth model differs in structure, so exact 0.90 is not expected. A ±3 SE band would be [0.88, 0.92].

text: A holdover forecast of 1000 runs shall complete within 2 seconds on the lab machine.
acceptance: C-FC-TIME: median wall time of 5 forecasts of 1000 runs is at most 2000 ms.
rationale: It runs inside the controller during an outage, possibly on battery.

text: The same model code shall run under run() and under runRealtime() with a fake clock and give identical traces.
acceptance: C-TWIN: 30 simulated days, trace arrays compared entry by entry (time, priority, kind, label), zero differences.
rationale: This is what lets offline verification say anything about the live controller. Spike: 5810 entries over 24 h, zero differences.
